---

## Learning goals

- Reconnect Bayes optimality $\Rightarrow$ “estimate densities from data”
- Run MLE for $V\sim\mathcal{N}(\theta,I)$ and get $\hat\theta=\bar V$
- See this as an **analytically solvable** case before mixtures / EM

---

## Before this clicks

MLE / min KL: $\hat\theta=\arg\max_\theta\frac{1}{n}\sum_i\log P_\theta(v_i)$.  
Bayes classifier needs posteriors / class-conditionals. Multivariate Gaussian density with mean $\theta\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$ and covariance $I$.

---

## Main ideas

### 1. Why density estimation now?

To implement the Bayes classifier you need $P(Y\mid X)$ or pieces that determine it: priors, class-conditionals $p(x\mid y)$, etc. So the algorithmic stretch of the course focuses on **estimating densities** (evaluation, not yet sampling / generation).

### 2. MLE template (again)

IID sample $v_1,\ldots,v_n$ from unknown $P_V$. Assume model $P_\theta$, maximize

$$
\mathcal{L}(\theta)=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\log P_\theta(v_i).
$$

### 3. Gaussian mean model

Assume

$$
P_\theta(v)=(2\pi)^{-d/2}\exp\Bigl(-\tfrac12\|v-\theta\|_{2}^{2}\Bigr),\qquad v\in\mathbb{R}^{d}
$$

(covariance fixed to $I$). Parameters: $\theta\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$.

Up to additive constants independent of $\theta$,

$$
\mathcal{L}(\theta)\;\propto\; -\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\|v_i-\theta\|_{2}^{2}.
$$

Set $\nabla_\theta\mathcal{L}=0$ $\Rightarrow$

$$
\hat\theta_{\mathrm{ML}}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}v_i.
$$

**Moral:** “take the sample average as the mean” is MLE / minimum KL under this Gaussian model — not a random habit.

### 4. Analytic vs numeric

Here differentiation works cleanly. Later (mixtures), $\log\sum_j(\cdots)$ blocks that cancellation; we will need iterative methods (EM).

### 5. Link to class-conditionals

Example story: model pixel vectors of an X-ray class as high-$d$ Gaussians; MLE mean $=$ average image in that class (under this simplified covariance).

---

## Worked mini-example

$d=1$, data $\{0,2,4\}$, model $\mathcal{N}(\theta,1)$.

$$
\hat\theta=\frac{0+2+4}{3}=2.
$$

Same as minimizing $\sum_i (v_i-\theta)^2$.

---

## Common confusions

| Confusion | Clarification |
|-----------|---------------|
| Sample mean is always “the” mean estimate | It is ML for this Gaussian mean model (covariance fixed) |
| We estimated the full Gaussian | Covariance was fixed to $I$; estimating $\Sigma$ is a similar but matrix exercise |
| Density estimation $=$ sampling | Here we care about evaluating $P_\theta(v)$; generative sampling is a later topic |
| Only unsupervised | Same algebra estimates a class-conditional if you restrict to one class’s samples |
